answer: To deter Sybil attacks in an agent economy managing a jade nursery garden, nodes authenticate peers via memory-hard proof-of-work challenges. Verifiers issue pseudorandom lookups across gigabyte-scale tables, forcing an attacker to buy dedicated physical DRAM channels per identity so a single server cannot harbor virtual nodes. However, memory-intensive hashing accelerates battery drain and thermal throttling, inducing latency spikes that trigger false authentication failures.
